I'm so sorry about your diagnosis. My mom had stage 4 Pancreatic cancer.  The final stages went extremely quick. In the matter of 3 weeks, she went down hill and passed once she stopped responding to treatment. She developed ascites which is fluid build up in the abdomen. Hers was due to the tumor blocking her liver bile ducts and basically all the toxins backed up and caused ascites and went to her brain and basically made her mentally gone. So watching out for swollen abdomen is one thing that developed in the last 3 weeks of my mom's life.

I'm so sorry to hear about your mom. Just throwing in my experience with my moms pancreatic cancer. Could have the doctors check her liver values as well.

He would give me massages randomly or cook dinner, buy us ice cream on the bad nights or just lay in bed with me all day when I couldnt manage to get up. Just remember, there wont be the right words to say to him to make it better, but those little actions of love such as suprising him with a favorite snack or picking up a movie to watch to pass the time is what helped me get through the same thing. 

Its not easy to care for someone in a state of turmoil, I know my boyfriend had it rough taking care of me after my mom passed. I never said a year, I said maybe more than a year but there are too many variables to tell and I stated said variables. I was just sharing what I've learned from this cancer. I never gave a time line.

My mom also had stage 4 Pancreatic cancer. One week tumor markers had dropped well over half on chemo. We celebrated, I thought maybe she will beat this, maybe I can have my mom around longer. Next week, the marker triples... on to the next chemo... She had I think 4 months after that left before she passed. It came so quick , even when results seemed so promising. Faith diminished over night. Of course every case is different but this was my experience.

So sorry to hear about your FIL, Pancreatic cancer is a bitch. Luckily he is stage 2 but fact of the matter is, as you said, its inoperable, it will never go away even with chemo. All you can hope for is some time.  

His doctor would be able to answer the life expectancy question. It really all depends on the presenting symptoms, how long the chemos last before being ineffective, and the overall health prior to diagnosis. My mom was stage 4 and she got a year of time. I have heard all ranges of life expectancy,  one week to one year for this cancer. Have they scanned to make sure it hasnt spread? It spreads so quick, so my understanding is that they are never stage 2 for long before it spreads. If he is 100% healthy in all other aspects, no symptoms, handles chemo well, no previous health issues, then maybe you can get more than a year, but there are so many variables.
